name: Prime Intellect Sandboxes

modes.label: VM sandbox, launch pricing (valid through 2026-12-22)
modes.note: PROMO launch list rates: $0.02/vCPU-h + $0.0125/GiB-h + $0.0002/GiB-h disk, billed while running on allocated resources (whole vCPUs 1-16, 128 MiB-64 GiB RAM, 2-128 GiB disk). A paused sandbox is billed for disk only. Valid through 2026-12-22; later rates unpublished. Granularity/minimum undocumented. 4 vCPU/8 GiB = $0.18/h (+$0.001/h for the default 5 GiB disk).

modes.label: GPU Pod marketplace, H100 80GB PCIe on-demand (cheapest live offer 2026-09-29: Lambda, all-in)
modes.note: Prime Intellect GPU Pods (separate product from Sandboxes). Live marketplace 2026-09-29 (public endpoint app.primeintellect.ai/api/trpc/availability.get, no login needed; dashboard 'Prices update in realtime'): cheapest 1x H100 80GB = Lambda PCIe us-west-3, $3.29/h all-in, 26 vCPU / 200 GB RAM / 1,024 GB disk; it was the only H100 offer and the dashboard showed 'H100 Unavailable' minutes earlier. No spot offers were listed (spotPrice null for every GPU type). The homepage tile ($2.43/hr, spot $0.94/hr, 32 vCPU/185 GB) is a static showcase, not the live listing. Some providers (e.g. Nebius) quote the GPU price only and add vCPU ($0.012/vCPU-h), RAM ($0.0032/GB-h) and disk ($0.0001/GB-h) on top; Lambda/Massed Compute offers are all-in. Credits deducted every minute while the Pod is active; pods are deleted when credits run out (FAQ). MARKETPLACE RATES FLUCTUATE by provider and stock.
modes.stock_note: marketplace: price and availability vary by provider

evidence.quote: block specific destinations and allow the rest with network_denylist=["evil.example.com"]
Run AI agents securely – restrict where code can reach with network allow/deny lists.

plans.name: Pay-as-you-go
plans.note: Tier-free: no subscription or minimum spend; prepaid Prime wallet. Default account limits: 1,024 active sandboxes, 4,096 vCPU, 4,096 GiB RAM total (so >4 vCPU per sandbox caps concurrency below 1,024), 32,768 GiB storage, 102,400 creations/h (burst 192/10 s); raisable via support. Timeout default 60 min, can be unlimited.

plans.name: Custom capacity
plans.note: Contact for more than the default limits ('tens of thousands' of concurrent sandboxes); pricing unpublished.

caveats: Rates are PROMOTIONAL launch list prices 'valid through December 22, 2026' (docs). Post-promo pricing is unpublished.
Billed on allocated vCPU/RAM/disk while running; 30% CPU utilisation saves nothing. Billing granularity and minimum are undocumented.

Pause/resume keeps memory, processes and disk on the same node, billed for disk only. The sandbox ends if that node is lost or a finite timeout runs out while paused. Sandboxes with volumes and GPU sandboxes cannot pause. Filesystem checkpoints ($0.10/GiB-month) and fork (files only) restore into a new sandbox; a checkpoint is lost if the source sandbox is deleted before it is DURABLE.
Idle timeout (optional, 1-1,440 min) TERMINATES the sandbox, it does not pause it; the default lifetime is 60 min (can be unlimited).
disk_gib_month 0.146 = $0.0002/GiB-h x 730 h. The disk is billed while running and while paused; it is deleted with the sandbox. The default 5 GiB disk costs ~$0.001/h.
The first VM launch of a new image converts it (PENDING for minutes, ~10 min per the verifiers docs); whether that time is billed is unknown.

GPU sandboxes (0-8 GPUs, VM-only) are coming soon and need a grant; no GPU types or prices are published. Prime's separate GPU Pods marketplace is modelled as the stock-flagged 'gpu-pod-h100' mode at the homepage H100 listing ($2.43/hr); actual price depends on the provider picked in the dashboard.
Hosted Evaluations on Prime Inference don't bill sandbox runtime separately (tokens only). Not modelled.

Inbound: an internet network rule publishes listed ports at https://<port>-<sandbox-id>.sandbox-v2-prod.pinfra.io. These URLs serve HTTP only and have no built-in auth. Raw TCP works only between sandboxes on a private network (<id>.sandbox.internal).

Secrets: env-var secrets land inside the VM; header secret injection keeps the value outside the VM for HTTPS (port 443) hosts you list, max 32 hosts, and the client must trust the Prime root CA. Egress rules are domain/IP only.
Preinstalled languages depend on the image you pick (default python:3.11-slim), so lang_* is null.
Egress price, regions and compliance certifications are undocumented (null).
Duplicate: cards/prime-intellect-sandboxes.json describes the same product with the same rates. Keep only one in the estimator.
Replaces an earlier stub card that wrongly said 'container' isolation with a separate beta VM mode. Docs: 'VM sandboxes are the default runtime'.
Launch pricing end date re-verified 2026-09-28 (docs sandboxes/overview: 'For our new launch, these rates are valid through December 22, 2026'); card price_expires = 2026-12-22 already set.

Prepaid wallet is non-refundable: Terms of Service 'All sales are final and no refund will be issued.' (support may issue credits for provider failures per FAQ). GPU Pods are auto-deleted when the wallet runs out.

GPU marketplace prices move in real time; the homepage GPU tiles are static marketing (e.g. H200 tiles showing '80 GB VRAM' at $0.47-$1.99/HR) and must not be used as rates. Use app.primeintellect.ai/api/trpc/availability.gpuSummary (public) for current cheapest per GPU.

Checkpoint storage (shared rate with VM images): $0.10/GiB-month billed hourly, plus a one-time upload charge equal to one day of storage when a checkpoint becomes DURABLE (not modelled; ~3% of a month).
SSH is shell/remote-command only: no port forwarding, agent forwarding, scp or sftp (use prime sandbox upload/download).

Volumes: named storage that outlives any sandbox, 100 GiB to 10 TiB, up to 8 per sandbox, published data billed as checkpoint storage. Writes are private to each sandbox until published; only sandboxes created later see a publish.

Browser: nothing preinstalled. verifiers BrowserEnv uses Browserbase (a separate paid service) as its documented browser provider, or boot an image with Chromium. No desktop or streamed screen is documented.

fleet.verification: Prime API key with sandbox permission and funded wallet for paid usage; further identity screening not published. GPU sandbox access needs explicit provider grant.
fleet.tiers: Entry per account 1,024 active sandboxes, 4,096 vCPU, 4,096 GiB RAM, 32,768 GiB storage; higher contact support.
fleet.notes: At 4 vCPU/8 GiB, memory limits concurrency to 512 before disk, despite 1,024 count. 10/50/300 fit resource pools at that size; 1,000 needs more memory quota. 102,400 creates/hour and burst 192/10sec are separate. GPU sandboxes coming soon/grant-gated, so default 0 means no initial access, not a post-approval quota.

snapshot_auto.quote: the pause saves the sandbox's disk as a checkpoint, which appears in `prime sandbox checkpoint list`.
snapshot_auto.note: Every pause checkpoints the disk automatically. Lifetime and idle timeouts still delete the sandbox without a checkpoint.

snapshot_on_demand.quote:
# 1. Create a checkpoint (prints its ID)
prime sandbox checkpoint create sbx_123
snapshot_on_demand.note: Manual checkpoint create/list/restore in CLI; SDK has checkpoint(), wait_for_checkpoint(), get_checkpoint(), list_checkpoints(). Restore starts a new sandbox (docker_image and disk_size_gb come from the checkpoint).

harness_api.quote: verifiers ships with a range of harnesses out of the box, including Claude Code, Codex, Pi, Prime-Agent,
harness_api.note: First-party open-source verifiers library (plus prime eval / Hosted Evaluations / prime-rl) runs Claude Code, Codex, OpenCode (OpenCodeEnv), mini-swe-agent etc. inside Prime sandboxes (runtime 'prime') with a task prompt and records traces live via an interception server. Batch eval/RL-oriented: no documented follow-up messages or conversation resume API.

egress_allowlist.quote: Both flags are repeatable and accept domains (`example.com`, `*.example.com`) or IPv4 addresses/CIDRs; IPv6 is not supported.
egress_allowlist.note: Allowlist or denylist (mutually exclusive), deny-all incl. DNS; replaceable on a running sandbox via `prime sandbox network`. Overview calls them 'VM-only egress controls'.

egress_http_rules.quote:
Schemes, credentials, ports, paths, query
    strings, bare ``*``, IPv6, and wildcards in other positions are rejected.
egress_http_rules.note: Egress entries are hostnames/IPv4/CIDR only; no method/path/header rules.

ingress_rules.quote: Anyone with the URL can connect. Prime does not authenticate these requests.
ingress_rules.note: Only the ports that an internet rule lists are exposed. Private networks use directed per-port TCP rules. Prime Tunnel (optional basic auth) is a separate tool. SSH via ephemeral-key `prime sandbox ssh`.

guest_firewall.note: Hardware-isolated microVM with its own guest kernel booting the OCI image as root filesystem; supports Docker/systemd/kernel-dependent workloads. Not documented explicitly.

secret_proxy.quote: The value never goes into the sandbox's environment, files, or configuration.
secret_proxy.note: Header secret injection adds stored secrets to HTTPS request headers outside the sandbox. Limits: HTTPS on port 443 only, 32 rule hosts per sandbox, clients must trust the Prime root certificate. Env-var secrets are a separate option.

volume_attach.quote: A volume is named storage that outlives any sandbox.
volume_attach.note: 100 GiB (default) to 10 TiB capacity; up to 8 mounts per sandbox with --volume NAME:/path[:ro]. Published volume data is billed as checkpoint storage ($0.10/GiB-month). A sandbox with a volume cannot pause.

volume_shared.quote: Its writes are invisible to every other sandbox, and a running sandbox never picks up later publishes.
volume_shared.note: No live shared volume. To share data, publish a volume version; sandboxes created after the publish see it.

anti_bot.quote: Sandboxes. Isolated microVM environments made for RL research.
anti_bot.note: not offered: outside the product's scope — Prime Sandboxes is a generic compute microVM for RL/agentic workloads, not a browser-automation product; no stealth/fingerprinting feature is documented.

captcha_solving.quote: Sandboxes. Isolated microVM environments made for RL research.
captcha_solving.note: not offered: outside the product's scope — no browser/CAPTCHA feature exists; Prime Sandboxes only exposes a generic Linux VM/CLI/SDK.

egress_ip_type.quote: VM sandboxes boot an OCI/Docker image as the root filesystem of a hardware-isolated microVM.
egress_ip_type.note: Derived: sandboxes run on Prime's own cloud/GPU-marketplace infrastructure with domain/IP allow-deny egress controls (cli.md); no residential or mobile IP product is offered or documented, so egress is ordinary datacenter IPs.

live_resize.quote: def create / def delete / def get / def list / def set_network / def execute_command
live_resize.note: CreateSandboxRequest fixes cpu_cores/memory_gb/disk_size_gb at creation; the SDK's SandboxClient exposes no resize/update/scale method (only create, delete, network updates, exec, file I/O). Changing size requires a new sandbox.

own_agent_api.quote: Prime Agent is an open-source coding and research agent for general and long-running work.
own_agent_api.note: not offered: outside the product's scope for Prime Sandboxes. Prime Agent is a coding/RLM harness (like Claude Code/Codex) that can run inside sandboxes and is already captured by agent_harnesses/harness_api; it is not a first-party API driving the provider's own browser/computer-use task agent as this field defines.

mcp_server.quote: Sandboxes Overview / Sandbox CLI Guide / Sandbox SDK Guide / Prime Images / Prime Tunnel
mcp_server.note: No MCP server is documented for controlling Prime Sandboxes; the org's public 'mcp-demo' repo is an empty RL-environments-over-MCP demo, unrelated to sandbox control, and no package.json/MCP entry exists in the prime-sandboxes package.

lang_python.note: not offered as a built-in default: docker_image is a required field with no default, so sandboxes only get a Python runtime if you choose a Python image (e.g. python:3.11-slim) yourself; nothing is preinstalled 'out of the box' regardless of image.

lang_node.note: not offered as a built-in default: same reasoning as lang_python — Node is only present if you pick a node:* image; the first-party SDK itself is Python-only (pyproject.toml, no package.json), so there is no first-party Node code-exec SDK either.

max_session_h.note: Per-sandbox lifetime timeout can be set to unlimited (cli.md: 'set the timeout to any negative value for no lifetime deadline'), so a sandbox can run indefinitely until you stop it.

persistent_disk.quote: a paused sandbox is billed only for its disk.
persistent_disk.note: The disk survives a pause. Filesystem checkpoints ($0.10/GiB-month) and named volumes also outlive the sandbox.

snapshot.quote: Pausing a sandbox saves its memory and disk on its node and stops the VM.
snapshot.note: Pause keeps memory and processes on the node. Checkpoints and forks are filesystem-only and outlive the source sandbox once DURABLE.

pause_resume.quote: Pausing a sandbox saves its memory and disk on its node and stops the VM.
pause_resume.note: Resume restores it in place with running processes and memory. A paused sandbox is billed for disk only. Limits: it stays on its node and ends if that node is lost; a finite timeout still runs while paused (the timeout can be unlimited); sandboxes with volumes and GPU sandboxes cannot pause.

fork.quote: The quickest way to branch a running sandbox is `fork`. It checkpoints the filesystem, waits for the checkpoint to be saved, and starts a new sandbox from it
fork.note: `prime sandbox fork sbx_123 --name experiment-branch --yes`; the fork inherits CPU, memory and timeout unless overridden.

fork_running.quote: A fork copies the filesystem, not the live session: it starts with the same files as the source, but processes start fresh and nothing in memory carries over.
fork_running.note: Forks a running sandbox, filesystem only.

memory_snapshot_fork.quote: Only files are restored: running processes and memory are not.
memory_snapshot_fork.note: Checkpoints and forks are filesystem-only. Pause keeps memory but resumes the same sandbox in place; it does not fork.

desktop.quote: Prime Sandboxes are disposable, isolated microVMs for AI-assisted coding, benchmarking, and quick experiments.
desktop.note: No desktop is preinstalled or streamed, and Prime documents no desktop/VNC example. Kept false.

browser.quote: Both modes use Browserbase (https://browserbase.com) as the browser provider.
browser.how: use the verifiers BrowserEnv, which drives a Browserbase browser (separate paid service), or boot a sandbox image that includes Chromium

computer_use.quote: CUA Mode: Vision-Based Control (Multimodal)... The CUA server template can forward `OPENAI_API_KEY` internally if it is present
computer_use.note: Screenshot+click 'CUA' mode is a verifiers-library harness pattern driving Browserbase, not a first-party computer-use API on Prime Sandboxes.

wake_on_request.quote: | Idle timeout | 1 min | 1,440 min (24 hr) | Disabled |
wake_on_request.note: Idle timeout terminates the sandbox; a paused sandbox resumes only on an explicit resume call, not on request.

volumes.quote: A volume is named storage that outlives any sandbox.

inbound_https.quote: Anyone with the URL can connect. Prime does not authenticate these requests.
inbound_https.note: An internet network rule publishes listed ports at https://<port>-<sandbox-id>.sandbox-v2-prod.pinfra.io. HTTP only, no built-in auth. Raw TCP works only between members of a private network.

public_ipv4.quote: Anyone with the URL can connect. Prime does not authenticate these requests.
public_ipv4.note: Public access is per-port HTTPS URLs on a shared Prime domain; no routable public IPv4 is assigned to a sandbox.

agent_harnesses.quote: Sandboxes run standard Docker images... Prime Image references always start with `prime/`.
agent_harnesses.note: Sandboxes boot whatever Docker image you bring; Prime does not ship preinstalled coding-agent images/templates (Claude Code, Codex, etc.) on the sandbox product itself. Those harnesses are run by the separate open-source `verifiers` library as user-supplied code inside a sandbox (see harness_api, already true), which is a different field.

gpu.quote: Our goal is to provision H100 GPU using availability data. First, we need to call the availability endpoint to get the current offers... We will use the Hyperstack provider and the following offer: {"cloudId": "n3-H100x1", "gpuType": "H100_80GB", ...}
gpu.note: This card already models a live GPU marketplace mode ('gpu-pod-h100', $3.29/h H100 offer confirmed against the public availability endpoint) for the same provider/id. Prime Intellect has a documented, working GPU provisioning API and marketplace (GPU Pods) today, not merely 'coming soon' -- only the separate VM-sandbox-integrated GPU feature is unreleased. Since the card's top-level `features.gpu` should reflect whether the provider offers GPU machines at all, and it does (via GPU Pods, already priced in this same card), false is incorrect; corrected to true.

windows.quote: VM sandboxes boot an OCI/Docker image as the root filesystem of a hardware-isolated microVM.
windows.note: Product boots Linux OCI/Docker images only; no Windows machine option is offered or documented anywhere in the sandbox/GPU docs.

macos.quote: VM sandboxes boot an OCI/Docker image as the root filesystem of a hardware-isolated microVM.
macos.note: Linux-only microVM/GPU cloud product; macOS is outside the product's scope, no macOS option anywhere in the docs.

arm64.quote: VM sandboxes boot an OCI/Docker image as the root filesystem of a hardware-isolated microVM.
arm64.note: No ARM/arm64/aarch64 instance type, image architecture flag, or GPU host is mentioned anywhere across sandboxes overview/cli/sdk/images docs, the API reference, or the prime-sandboxes SDK source (only x86_64 GPU hosts like H100/H200 appear, and default images like python:3.11-slim/ubuntu:22.04 are used without any arch selector). No architecture choice is exposed at all, implying a single (x86_64) architecture; reasoned false rather than null.

self_host.quote: Track usage limits and billing inside the [Prime Billing dashboard](https://app.primeintellect.ai/dashboard/billing).
self_host.note: Sandboxes/GPU Pods are a hosted SaaS with billing/wallet through Prime's own dashboard; no on-prem/self-hosted deployment of the sandbox runtime is documented.

byoc.quote: Sandboxes are billed while running. For our new launch, these rates are valid through December 22, 2026
byoc.note: Prime runs and bills sandboxes on its own infrastructure/marketplace; no bring-your-own-cloud-account deployment option is documented.

open_source.quote: Track usage limits and billing inside the [Prime Billing dashboard](https://app.primeintellect.ai/dashboard/billing).
open_source.note: The Sandboxes/GPU Pods runtime and dashboard are closed, billed SaaS. (Prime does open-source separate tooling like the `verifiers` library and `prime-rl`, but that is not the sandbox/compute product itself.)

nested_virt.quote: VM sandboxes boot an OCI/Docker image as the root filesystem of a hardware-isolated microVM.
nested_virt.note: Not documented either way. No mention of /dev/kvm, nested virtualization, or running VMs/emulators inside a sandbox anywhere in the docs, CLI/SDK reference, or GitHub source; hardware-isolated microVMs (the described architecture) typically do not expose nested KVM to the guest unless explicitly advertised, which it is not here. Reasoned false rather than null.

static_egress_ip.quote: Both flags are repeatable and accept domains (`example.com`, `*.example.com`) or IPv4 addresses/CIDRs; IPv6 is not supported.
static_egress_ip.note: Egress is controlled via allow/deny lists of destination domains/IPs, not by giving the sandbox a fixed outbound IP address. No 'static IP', 'egress IP', or 'outbound IP' feature is mentioned anywhere in the docs; card already records network.ipv4_available=false and public_ipv4=false, consistent with no dedicated/static IP being assigned to a sandbox at all (inbound or outbound).

soc2.quote: PrimeIntellect holds a SOC 2 Type 1 attestation report for its AI Compute Platform System as of August 15, 2026, issued by an independent service auditor, which evaluates the suitability of the design of controls based on the Security trust services criteria.
soc2.note: Visible Compliance section lists SOC 2 Type 1 and SOC 2 Type 2; the page's embedded SafeBase data still gives Type 1 maturity "full" (auditor Insight Assurance, quote above) and Type 2 maturity "in_progress". Documents lists only the SOC 2 Type 1 report.

hipaa.quote: PrimeIntellect holds a SOC 2 Type 1 attestation report for its AI Compute Platform System as of August 15, 2026
hipaa.note: not offered: the Trust Center's certifications section shows only SOC 2 Type 1 (attained) and SOC 2 Type 2 (in progress) as actually-held items; no HIPAA/BAA attestation is listed anywhere on the Trust Center, security page, or docs.

sso.quote: We've introduced a "Teams" feature where you can invite multiple users and set a dedicated billing email.
sso.note: not offered: Teams support is limited to inviting members and setting a billing email; no SAML/OIDC/SSO, identity-provider integration, or enterprise directory sync is documented anywhere in the docs. The Trust Center's 'single sign on' line is generic hidden-section placeholder copy, not a confirmed feature.

eu_data_residency.note: Prime's GPU Pods marketplace (modelled in this same card as the 'gpu-pod-h100' mode) exposes eu_east/eu_north/eu_west as filterable/provisionable regions via the availability and provisioning API, so GPU machines can be kept in the EU. The VM-sandbox product (the 'on-demand' mode) does not document any region selector at all in overview/cli/sdk, so it is unclear whether Sandboxes themselves can be pinned to an EU region; this answer is driven by the GPU Pods side of the card.

usage_api.quote: Track usage limits and billing inside the Prime Billing dashboard
usage_api.note: granularity: account-only; cost: no; Prime Intellect tracks sandbox costs and credits through a web dashboard (app.primeintellect.ai/dashboard/billing) only. Billing is calculated server-side based on allocated vCPU-hours and RAM-hours, but no REST API or CLI command exists to programmatically retrieve billable usage or cost per sandbox or per tag. Usage granularity is account-wide (wallet level) with no breakdown by individual sandbox via any API endpoint.

ssh.quote: Only interactive shells and remote commands are supported: port forwarding (`-L`/`-R`), agent forwarding, `scp`, and `sftp` are not. Use `prime sandbox upload` / `download` to move files.
ssh.note: SSH via `prime sandbox ssh` with an ephemeral key per session; SSH sessions do not count as activity for the idle timeout.

persist_scope.quote: Resuming restores it in place: running processes, open files, and in-memory state carry on from the moment of the pause.
persist_scope.note: Pause keeps the whole disk and memory on the same node, billed for disk only ($0.0002/GiB-h). The sandbox ends if that node is lost or a finite timeout runs out. Sandboxes with volumes or GPUs cannot pause.

private_network.quote: Each member is reachable from the others at `<sandbox-id>.sandbox.internal`
private_network.note: Private networks between VM sandboxes of the same team or owner, with per-port TCP rules and localhost forwards.

credential_injection.quote: The value never goes into the sandbox's environment, files, or configuration.

locations_quote: Query Parameters: regions - List[string] - Filter by region(s) (e.g., united_states, canada, europe_west)
